prompt: Using the same $f(x) = x + 4$ and $g(x) = 3x$, find $g(f(2))$.
hint: This time $f$ is on the inside, so $f$ runs FIRST and $g$ works on its result.

hints.text: This time $f$ is on the inside, so $f$ runs FIRST and $g$ works on its result.
Start inside: $f(2) = 2 + 4 = 6$. Then put that $6$ into $g$, which multiplies by $3$.

explanation: The inside machine always goes first, and here the inside machine is $f$.
The function $f$ adds $4$ to its input, so the inside value is $f(2) = 2 + 4 = 6$.
Then $g$ triples that result: $g(6) = 18$. This differs from $f(g(2)) = 10$, so the order matters, and the answer is $18$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Swap the machines on the belt
steps: Put the "add 4" machine first: 2 goes in, 6 comes out.
Then the "triple it" machine: 6 goes in, 18 comes out.
Same two machines, different order, different answer.
